waypoints.name: Holden Village / Railroad Creek Trailhead
waypoints.note: Access via Lady of the Lake ferry to Lucerne then the Holden Village shuttle bus; standard-route parties stage here.
waypoints.directions: There is no road in. Take the Lake Chelan ferry from Chelan or Field's Point to Lucerne, then the village shuttle up from the landing. Plan the whole trip around the boat and bus timetable in both directions — parties who miss the connection out spend an extra night at the village.

waypoints.name: Railroad Creek Trail / Holden Lake Trail junction
waypoints.note: Leave the valley-bottom trail here and climb toward Holden Lake on dry, open-pine switchbacks.
waypoints.directions: Walk the gravel road and Railroad Creek Trail (FST 1256) west out of the village for about a mile. The Holden Lake Trail leaves it on the right and is signed.

waypoints.name: Holden Lake
waypoints.note: Common base camp in a glacial basin directly below the Mary Green Glacier; water is scarce on the approach so fill up here.
waypoints.directions: Steady climbing for several miles through forest and brush, with a few small side creeks that run reliably. Black flies are thick through the lower part of this stretch. The trail ends in the cirque directly under Bonanza's east face.

waypoints.name: Holden Pass high camp
waypoints.note: Alternate, higher camp that most summit parties use to shorten summit day; some brushy bushwhacking to reach it.
waypoints.directions: From the lake outlet the tread fades out. Skirt the north shore through slide alder and talus — genuine bushwhacking and route-finding, worse early season when the water is high — then climb a hillside traverse northwest to the pass.

waypoints.name: Mary Green Glacier, north edge
waypoints.note: Rising traverse to a snowfield below slabs, then a scramble onto the glacier's north edge — rope up for the crossing here.
waypoints.directions: Rising traverse west from the pass along the ridge and slope to a snowfield beneath rock slabs at roughly 7,000 to 7,300 ft. Scramble the class 3 slabs above it, starting high and to the right to keep clear of a waterfall. The gullies here sit below a retreating glacier margin and are loose, so stay out of the fall line and out from under any party above you.

waypoints.name: Moat crossing, glacier's upper corner
waypoints.note: Cross the moat via a snow bridge onto rock; bridges can collapse by late season, sometimes forcing a detour right onto rock.
waypoints.directions: Bear west along the glacier's north (climber's right) edge, then traverse southwest under the base of Bonanza's northeast ridge to the glacier's upper corner. Finish up the steep snow finger to its high point and look for the exit onto rock; an overhanging snow lip can be as much of an obstacle as the moat itself. The crossing gets harder as the season goes on and can turn into a maze of crevasses rather than a single step across.

waypoints.name: Bonanza Peak summit
waypoints.note: True summit reached after the moat and a short Class 3-4 finish; descent reverses the route with about four rappels off fixed stations.
waypoints.directions: Off the snow, climb class 3-4 rock just right of a gully for several rope-lengths, then traverse left into a second gully and scramble to a notch on the northeast ridge just north of the top. From the notch follow the crest past a run of large blocks to the summit horn. The rock along here is loose and this is where the route's rockfall problem lives — anything knocked off funnels straight down the gullies onto whoever is below.

waypoints.name: Stuart Lake Trailhead
waypoints.directions: Follow Icicle Creek Road to FR-7601 and take it to its end at the Stuart Lake Trailhead, about 3,400 ft. Everything above starts on foot from here, on Stuart Lake Trail #1599.

waypoints.name: Fryingpan Creek Trailhead
waypoints.note: Wonderland Trail junction near the White River entrance, Mount Rainier NP.

waypoints.name: Little Tahoma Summit
waypoints.note: Via Fryingpan Glacier, Whitman Notch (~9100 ft), and the Whitman Glacier to the East Ridge; glacier permit required.

waypoints.name: Stuart Lake Trailhead
waypoints.directions: Drive Eightmile Road (FR-7601) to its end at the Stuart Lake/Colchuck Lake trailhead, about 3,500 ft. Overnight stays in the Colchuck Zone need a quota wilderness permit.

waypoints.name: Colchuck Lake
waypoints.directions: Follow the Stuart Lake Trail #1599 about 2.5 miles to the signed fork where the Colchuck Lake Trail #1599.1 splits left and south. Continue roughly 1.8 miles more, crossing Mountaineer Creek and a boulder-hop stretch near the outlet, to the lake at 5,570 ft. This is the last easy, reliable water, so fill here because there is none above.

waypoints.name: Aasgard Pass
waypoints.directions: Skirt the lake's south and east shoreline on a braided, cairned climbers' path over talus and slab to the foot of the obvious steep gully and headwall at the head of the lake. Aasgard gains roughly 2,000 ft in under a mile on dirt switchbacks, loose scree and boulder-hopping; cairns get knocked over and the path splits into several use trails, so keep re-picking the line toward the notch. Firm snow and ice can linger into July, making an axe and sometimes crampons worthwhile on what is otherwise a scramble.

waypoints.name: Core Enchantments
waypoints.directions: From the pass, cross the grey talus and glacial till of the upper Core Zone past Tranquil Lake (Lake Freya) and Isolation Lake, then drop slightly into the meadow-and-tarn complex sometimes called the Brisingamen Lakelets.

waypoints.name: Base of south slopes
waypoints.directions: Near the far end of the meadows, watch for an unsigned climbers' path forking right, to the west, toward Little Annapurna. If you cross a stream and pass a toilet sign you have gone by the junction and should backtrack.

waypoints.name: Little Annapurna summit
waypoints.directions: Above here it is a scatter of cairned, well-worn boot paths rather than a trail. Take the line of least resistance up the broad south-facing slabs and talus on the peak's east side, switchbacking and scrambling at low 3rd class at most. The true summit is the middle of three rocky high points along the crest.

waypoints.name: Fryingpan Creek crossing
waypoints.note: Wonderland Trail crosses Fryingpan Creek on a footbridge in old-growth forest before switchbacking up toward Summerland; last easy creek water below treeline.

waypoints.name: Summerland
waypoints.note: Subalpine meadow camp with a stone shelter below Little Tahoma's east face; a reserved wilderness permit is required to camp here, and it's the jumping-off point for the climbing route.

waypoints.name: Toe of Fryingpan Glacier
waypoints.note: Leave the Wonderland Trail and climb steep talus/heather slopes to gain the lower edge of the Fryingpan Glacier; route-finding through boulders, often snow-covered into midsummer.

waypoints.name: Whitman Notch
waypoints.note: The obvious low point in the ridge just left of Little Tahoma; cross here from the Fryingpan Glacier onto the Whitman Glacier.

waypoints.name: Whitman Glacier bergschrund
waypoints.note: Crevasses and a bergschrund open up on the Whitman Glacier below the summit pyramid; rope up and probe for hidden slots, especially in low-snow years.

waypoints.name: East shoulder saddle
waypoints.note: Gain the saddle on Little Tahoma's east shoulder, a narrow crumbly-andesite rib with roughly 2,000 ft of exposure down to the Emmons Glacier on the north side.

waypoints.name: Fryingpan Creek / Summerland Trailhead
waypoints.note: White River Road ~2.9 mi past the White River entrance turnoff, just beyond the Fryingpan Creek bridge; this is the sole approach for the standard Fryingpan Glacier–Whitman Glacier–East Ridge/East Shoulder route via Summerland and Meany Crest.

waypoints.name: Tucquala Meadows Trailhead
waypoints.note: FS 4330 (Cle Elum Valley Rd), ~13 mi past Salmon-la-Sac. Standard access for Peggys Pond via Cathedral Pass Trail #1345 to Cathedral Pass, continuing to Mount Daniel's SE slopes/Daniel Glacier.
waypoints.directions: Drive up the Cle Elum River valley on Forest Service Road 4330 (Cle Elum Valley Road), about 13 miles past Salmon-la-Sac, to its end at the trailhead, roughly 3,400 feet. The access road is rough gravel and is best driven with a high-clearance or 4x4 vehicle.

waypoints.name: Cascade Pass Trailhead (end of Cascade River Road)
waypoints.note: Also the standard trailhead for the reverse Ptarmigan Traverse exit at Downey Creek is different (Suiattle River Rd), but Cascade Pass is the traditional/most common starting trailhead.

waypoints.name: Cascade Pass
waypoints.note: Maintained trail ends here; traverse continues cross-country.

waypoints.name: Cache Col
waypoints.note: Glacier-travel notch south of Cascade Pass; gateway to the traverse proper.

waypoints.name: Kool-Aid Lake
waypoints.note: First bivy; the exposed 'Red Ledges' traverse below Art's Knoll follows.

waypoints.name: Red Ledges (Art's Knoll)
waypoints.note: Narrow, exposed ledge crossing; a fall here would be serious.

waypoints.name: Yang-Yang Lakes
waypoints.note: Second common bivy, below Spider-Formidable Col.

waypoints.name: Spider-Formidable Col
waypoints.note: High col crossing toward the LeConte Glacier and Sentinel/Old Guard Peaks.

waypoints.name: White Rock Lakes / South Cascade Glacier Col
waypoints.note: Third bivy; crosses the flat South Cascade Glacier en route to Spire Point.

waypoints.name: Spire Point
waypoints.note: Prominent landmark near the Dome-Dana col.

waypoints.name: Cub Lake / Itswoot Ridge
waypoints.note: Fourth bivy on Itswoot Ridge above Cub and Itswoot Lakes.

waypoints.name: Dome Peak
waypoints.note: Optional side summit near the traverse's south end; the traverse itself does not cross it.

waypoints.name: Thunder Creek Trailhead, Colonial Creek Campground
Rainy Pass Trailhead (SR 20)
waypoints.note: Northwest Forest Pass required; parking is at the Rainy Pass picnic area, trailhead sign at the north end of the lot.

waypoints.name: Heather Pass junction
waypoints.note: Leave the Lake Ann/Maple Pass Loop trail #740 here onto the unmaintained climbers' path toward Lewis and Wing Lakes.

waypoints.name: Talus field crossings
waypoints.note: Two loose talus fields to cross on the climbers' path before Lewis Lake; cairned but easy to lose in fog.

waypoints.name: Lewis Lake
waypoints.note: Lower, less-established camp option; only a couple of decent tent spots on the north shore.

waypoints.name: Wing Lake outlet
waypoints.note: Reliable water; the lake outlet is the last dependable source before the summit push.

waypoints.name: Wing Lake camp
waypoints.note: Standard base camp for Black Peak climbers; best established tent sites are here rather than Lewis Lake.

waypoints.name: South col
waypoints.note: Gained via a moraine and permanent snowfield east of Wing Lake; a broad gully on the west side leads to the summit blocks.

waypoints.name: Black Peak summit
waypoints.note: Class 3 with easy class 4 moves near the top; helmet recommended for rockfall off the summit block.
